title: iPhone Duo goes on sale — Apple's first foldable, supply-capped, six days before the est. FQ4 print
source: NEWS: Apple's own newsroom press release 'Apple unveils iPhone Duo' (apple.com/newsroom/2026/09/apple-unveils-iphone-duo/), fetched direct 2026-09-10, states pre-orders begin Friday, October 16 with availability beginning Friday, October 23 in more than 70 countries and regions, and in 28 other countries and regions beginning Friday, October 30; US pricing starts at $1,999 for 256GB and runs to $3,199 for 2TB. Corroborated the same day by MacRumors ('iPhone Duo: Pricing, Pre-Orders, and Release Date Announced', 2026-09-09), AppleInsider (2026-09-09) and Variety (2026-09-09). Filed `estimate` on the two counts this calendar has documented before: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot a proposal may claim, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. THE DATE IS NOT IN DOUBT — the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence; the lane that writes the canonical file should promote it against apple.com/newsroom directly, which is an IR: source
notes: Discovered during the aapl-iphone-18-launch-2026-09-09 close-out (2026-09-10). WHY THIS IS PROPOSED AT ALL, since it departs from a ruling the proposing ledger made four times: that ledger ruled at D-21 that pre-order and on-sale dates are 'launch sub-milestones, not market events', and upheld it at D-5, D-3 and D-1. That ruling is KEPT for the iPhone 18 Pro's 09-12 pre-order and 09-18 on-sale, and for the Duo's own 10-16 pre-order. It is departed from for 10-23 on three grounds the earlier rows could not weigh because the facts did not exist yet: (1) it is a NEW PRODUCT CATEGORY's first availability — Apple's first foldable — not the annual refresh of an existing line; (2) it is FIVE WEEKS DETACHED from the 09-09 keynote with its own pre-order cycle and its own two-wave country rollout, so it is a separate dated event rather than a milestone of that one; (3) it lands SIX DAYS BEFORE the estimated 2026-10-29 FQ4 print, which is where the launch's real P/L settles per that ledger's standing thesis, and with supply rather than demand the binding constraint the 10-23 sell-through and lead-time tape is the last read available before the FQ1 guide. THE SUPPLY CONSTRAINT IS THE WHOLE POINT: Nikkei Asia (2026-09-04) put early foldable output at 'a few hundred' units a day in late August on surface-flatness and hinge yields against an order book raised to ~10M/yr, and the five-week stagger plus a second country wave on 10-30 is what Apple's own dating looks like under that constraint. Evercore ISI's Amit Daryanani (Buy, PT $365, 2026-09-10) states it directly — Apple 'will sell as many units as it can manufacture in the first six months', supply not demand binding through the first half of the sales cycle. Unit models are unusually dispersed and that dispersion is itself the reason to track the date: TD Cowen ~6M units 2H26, Goldman Sachs 14M base to 35M optimistic for 2026, Melius up to 15M for FY2027, Morgan Stanley ~$14B of December-quarter Duo revenue. Filed `medium`, not `high`, to match the proposing event's own tier: a single device's on-sale day moves AAPL through information about the FQ1 guide, not through its own tape, and no dated resolution of the supply question is scheduled. If the lane that researches this id disagrees with the departure above, the proposal is inert and costs nothing — which is precisely why it is a proposal and not a canonical file.
